params.question: A 22-year-old construction worker sustains a comminuted intra-articular tibial plateau fracture in a road traffic accident. Which of the following best explains why this particular injury warrants a structured prognosis counselling conversation?

answers.text: All fractures seen in the emergency department require formal prognosis counselling regardless of severity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Not all fractures require structured prognosis counselling. It is specifically indicated when the injury will impose a significant, lasting burden on the patient's physical function, livelihood, or quality of life — simple fractures that heal without residual disability do not meet this threshold.

answers.text: Intra-articular fractures routinely result in post-traumatic arthritis and lasting functional disability that affects the patient's livelihood

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Intra-articular fractures of the tibial plateau, calcaneus, and distal femur commonly lead to post-traumatic arthritis and residual disability — one of the four broad clinical categories that consistently require structured prognosis conversations in orthopaedics.

answers.text: Tibial plateau fractures invariably require limb amputation, necessitating consent counselling

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tibial plateau fractures do not invariably require amputation. The counselling need arises from the high risk of residual joint stiffness, chronic pain, and functional disability — not from amputation risk.

answers.text: Prognosis counselling is indicated only when the patient specifically requests information about their recovery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prognosis counselling should be clinician-initiated whenever the natural course of the condition will impose significant functional or livelihood burden. A young labourer facing permanent work disability needs proactive counselling even if he does not ask for it.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four broad categories: fractures with residual disabilities, fractures requiring prolonged bed stay, bone tumours, and congenital disabilities. The common thread is a significant, lasting burden on physical function, livelihood, or quality of life.

Well done. Intra-articular fractures with residual disability are a classic indication for structured prognosis counselling — the impact on livelihood and quality of life demands the same careful communication as a life-threatening diagnosis.

params.question: An 8-year-old boy presents with high fever, localised tibial tenderness, and refusal to bear weight. You suspect acute osteomyelitis and need to convince his parents to accept urgent referral to a higher centre. According to the five-part referral counselling structure, what should be your first step?

answers.text: Reassure the parents that the condition is not serious but a specialist opinion would be helpful

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Downplaying the severity with hedging language undermines the clinical imperative for timely referral. Families who do not understand the urgency are far more likely to delay or refuse transfer — leading to the delayed presentations that dominate district hospital morbidity.

answers.text: Discuss the estimated cost of treatment at the referral centre so the family can arrange finances

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Addressing financial concerns is important but comes later in the referral conversation. The first step must establish what has been found and why it is urgent — without this foundation, the family has no frame for evaluating any practical consideration.

answers.text: Name the clinical finding explicitly and state its significance without hedging language

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Step 1 of the five-part structure is to name the finding and its significance directly — for example: 'I have examined your son carefully and I am concerned he may have a bone infection that can cause serious, permanent damage if not treated promptly at a facility with surgical capability.'

answers.text: Provide a written referral letter and advise the family to proceed at their convenience

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Handing over a referral letter without a structured counselling conversation leads to poor compliance. The referral conversation must first build the family's understanding of the urgency before any documentation is provided.

overallFeedback.feedback: The five-part referral structure follows this sequence: (1) name the finding and its significance, (2) explain why local management is insufficient, (3) describe what the higher centre offers, (4) address the family's fears and practical barriers, (5) arrange the logistics. Step 1 comes first because it establishes the urgency that motivates everything else.
Excellent. Beginning with an explicit, unhesitating statement of the finding and its significance sets the tone for the entire referral conversation and communicates clinical urgency.

interactions.label: A 55-year-old patient with peripheral vascular disease has undergone a below-kne

params.question: A 55-year-old patient with peripheral vascular disease has undergone a below-knee amputation. During post-operative counselling about the rehabilitation ahead, which of the following most accurately describes what the patient should expect?

answers.text: Rehabilitation requires only the orthopaedic surgeon and a prosthetist working together

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Successful amputation rehabilitation is multidisciplinary. No single clinician or pair of clinicians can deliver the full spectrum of care — surgeons, rehabilitation physicians, physiotherapists, prosthetists, psychologists, and social workers all contribute essential elements.

answers.text: A definitive prosthesis can be fitted within two weeks of surgery, and independent walking resumes within one month

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Premature prosthetic fitting risks stump complications. The staged programme includes wound healing, pre-prosthetic conditioning, initial prosthetic fitting, gait training, and community reintegration — this takes at minimum six months, not weeks.

answers.text: Rehabilitation focuses solely on prosthetic gait training, as psychological adjustment occurs naturally over time

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The emotional and identity impact of limb loss demands professional psychological support. A patient who arrives at their first prosthetic appointment without adequate psychological preparation is significantly more likely to abandon rehabilitation entirely.

answers.text: The journey to independent community walking involves at minimum six months of staged rehabilitation with coordinated input from surgeons, therapists, prosthetists, and psychologists

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Amputation rehabilitation requires at minimum six months of coordinated multidisciplinary input across defined stages — from wound healing through prosthetic fitting to community reintegration. A patient who understands this structured timeline is far more likely to sustain engagement through the difficult early weeks.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key points are: rehabilitation takes at minimum six months, follows defined stages with clear milestones, and requires coordinated input from surgeons, rehabilitation physicians, physiotherapists, prosthetists, psychologists, and social workers. No single clinician can deliver it alone.

Well done. Understanding the realistic timeline and the multidisciplinary nature of amputation rehabilitation is essential for setting patient expectations and sustaining engagement through a long recovery.
